1.text: Welcome to ACI Advanced Characterization and Instrumentation.

2.text: Before introducing ACI in more detail, this slide provides a quick overview of the ISCE² organizational structure. Here, you can see where ACI sits within the Institute. ACI is led by our Division Director, Andrew Lim. In the next few slides, I will introduce our team and highlight the key analytical capabilities and shared scientific resources that we offer.

3.text: ACI is organised into three technical domains, chromatography and mass spectrometry, X-ray spectroscopy and microscopy, and NMR, physical and thermal characterisation. Together, our domain leads and staff manage a broad range of shared scientific resources and provide analytical and characterisation support, as well as technical training, to our research community. Beyond supporting our internal R&D activities, we also extend our capabilities to industry partners, providing services such as material characterisation, failure diagnostics, method development, consultancy, and collaboration. Through these capabilities, we aim to provide practical analytical solutions to support different research and industry needs.

4.text: The ACI division is led by our division director, Andrew Lim, and Ong Li Li as the Division Deputy Director. And it comprises three technical domains, each led by our respective domain lead. The Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry domain is led by Mr. Ong Wai Chung, supported by our instrument specialists, Ng Fu Song and Tan Kuan Yi. The X-ray Spectroscopy and Microscopy domain is led by Ms. Angeline Seo, together with three senior domain specialists, Wang Zhan, Chia Sze Chen, and Cao Xun, who specialize in XPS, XRD and TEM respectively. Ong Li Li also served as the domain lead of NMR, Physical and Thermal Characterisation, supported by instrument specialists Yeo Wen Cong and Kuan Kai Cong. Beyond our analytical and characterisation work, ACI also plays an important role in managing shared scientific resources across the Institute. Our responsibilities include equipment booking, utilisation and charging, demand aggregation, scientific equipment and systems refresh, and equipment lifecycle management. We also support digitalisation and sustainability initiatives. Together, these activities help ensure that our scientific resources are effectively managed, optimised, and kept relevant to support the evolving research needs across the Institute.

5.text: This slide gives you an overview of where our ACI laboratories are located within the Institute. Our eight analytical laboratories are conveniently located together on level 1. Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry is based in Lab 1-01. X-ray spectroscopy and microscopy is located in Labs 1-02, 1-03 and 1-06, while NMR Physical and Thermal Characterisation is based in Labs 1-04 and 1-05. Labs 1-07 and 1-08 are shared laboratories with other R&D divisions. Having our analytical capabilities located close to one another makes it easier for our teams to provide integrated analytical support for a wide range of research needs.

6.text: Let's now take a closer look at our three technical domains, starting with chromatography and mass spectrometry. This domain brings together three key areas, gas chromatography, liquid chromatography, and mass spectrometry. These complementary techniques allow us to separate, identify, and analyze a wide range of chemical compounds, supporting both routine testing and more complex analytical investigations. In the following slides, I will briefly introduce some of the key analytical capabilities and instrumentation available within this domain.

7.text: Within this domain, we have a broad range of instruments to support different analytical needs. For gas chromatography, our capabilities include conventional GC with TCD and FID detectors, comprehensive two-dimensional GC, or GC×GC, as well as GC-MS equipped with pyrolysis, which can be used for microplastic analysis, thermal desorption, and headspace capabilities. We also have a refinery gas analyzer with a grab sampling system for gas analysis. For liquid chromatography, we have HPLC systems equipped with different detectors. We also have GPC systems using either THF or aqueous system, depending on the solubility of the samples. Our combustion ion chromatography capability supports the quantification of halogens, anions and cations in solid, liquid, and gas samples. For more advanced mass spectrometry, we have LC-QTOF-MS and high-resolution LC-MS/MS using the Q Exactive Orbitrap, supporting both targeted and non-targeted analysis. Finally, for elemental analysis, we have ICP-MS and ICP-OES, supported by microwave digestion for sample preparation.

8.text: Moving on to our second technical domain, X-ray Spectroscopy and Microscopy, led by Ms. Angeline Seo. Here, you can see some of the key instruments available within this domain. We have SEM and TEM, which allow us to examine the morphology and structure of materials at very small length scales. We also have SAXS and WAXS for studying material structures and XPS for surface elemental and chemical analysis. In addition, our Powder X-ray diffractometer is equipped with a reaction chamber for in situ XRD studies, allowing us to monitor structural changes under reaction conditions. We also have XRF with mapping capability for elemental analysis and distribution. Together, these instruments provide complementary information on the morphology, structure, surface chemistry, and elemental composition of different materials.

9.text: Looking more closely to this domain, we can broadly group our instruments into three areas. For X-ray characterisation, we have powder X-ray diffraction with an in-situ reaction chamber, X-ray fluorescence with mapping capability, as well as small and wide-angle X-ray scattering, or SAXS and WAXS. For electron microscopy, we have SEM with EDS and BEX capabilities. and TEM with advanced capabilities including Cryo-TEM, EDS, 3D tomography and EELS. We also have 3D X-ray micro-CT and atomic force microscopy, allowing us to examine materials across different length scales. For surface and molecular characterisation, we have XPS and Raman spectroscopy, both with in situ gas reaction capabilities.

10.text: Moving on to our third technical domain, NMR, physical and thermal characterisation. Our capabilities can broadly be divided into two areas. The first is Nuclear Magnetic Resonance, or NMR, where we have liquid-state NMR spectrometers for molecular structure identification, structural characterisation, and quantitative analysis. The second is our thermal, chemical, and physical characterisation laboratory. which houses a wide range of instruments for evaluating the thermal behavior, physical properties, and other characteristics of different materials. Together, these capabilities allow us to look at materials from both a molecular and bulk property perspective, providing complementary information to support research, product development, and problem solving.

11.text: Looking more closely at third domain, our capabilities can be broadly grouped into three areas. First, for NMR, we have liquid-state NMR spectrometers equipped with both iProbe and cryoprobe, supporting molecular structure characterisation and quantitative analysis. The second area is chemical and physical characterisation, where we have a wide range of instruments for measuring different material properties. These include surface area and pore size, particle size, rheology, spectroscopy, dispersion and stability, as well as mechanical and thermal conductivity measurements. The third area is thermal analysis, where our capabilities include TPDRO, simultaneous DSC-TGA and DSC, allowing us to study how materials behave and change under controlled temperature conditions. Together, these complementary techniques allow us to characterize materials from their molecular structure through to their physical, chemical, and thermal properties, giving us a more comprehensive understanding of the samples we analyze.

12.text: To summarize, this slide brings together the wide range of analytical capabilities available within ACI across our three technical domains. With this broad range of complementary techniques, we are able to support different types of samples and analytical needs. More importantly, our team can work with you to identify the most appropriate analytical approach for your specific research needs.
